title: Features: a requirement is off
summary: DJDL's Settings → Features with Licensing and Sign-in off: Commerce's switch is disabled with 'Needs Licensing. Turn it on first.', a Turn on Licensing link and the same words as its tooltip; Cloud Sync is disabled the same way because Sign-in is off (Managed config, its other requirement, is on); and the sidebar has no Licensing, Sign-in, Cloud Sync or Commerce group.
compare: The owner rule, drawn: a service can be turned on only when its requirements are on. Its switch is disabled (aria-disabled, still focusable) and its tooltip and line say the same thing: what to turn on first.

The requirement line names each unmet requirement and the next step ('Needs Licensing. Turn it on first.'); for two requirements it marks the one that is met ('Needs Managed config (on) and Sign-in. Turn on Sign-in first.'). Requirements come from tools/services.json.
Turn on Licensing / Turn on Sign-in scroll to and focus that row's switch; they don't turn anything on by themselves. The server refuses the dependent too (commerce_requires_license).
A feature that is off hides its nested rows (Sign-in's Customer portal); a requirement that is off still says what needs it ('Commerce needs it').
The sidebar shows groups only for features that are on.
Phone: the tooltip shows on long-press; the line and link wrap under the description; switches keep their 24 px hit area.
